newsitem.title: CANADA: Oil prices, gas wars squeeze Petro-Can Q3.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices, gas wars squeeze Petro-Can Q3.

text.p: Petro-Canada on Thursday closed the parade of weak third-quarter results in Canada's integrated oil sector by reporting sharply lower earnings due to high crude oil prices and gasoline price wars.

Petro-Canada, following lower returns by Suncor Inc, Shell Canada Ltd and Imperial Oil Ltd, said third-quarter net earnings fell to C$24 million or C$0.08 a share from C$79 million or C$0.32 a share last year.
Revenues in the period climbed to C$359 million from C$308 million.

Although the company made strategic and operational gains in the third quarter, it faced the highest oil prices since the Gulf War, which squeezed refining margins, and gasoline wars in Quebec that lowered returns, said Petro-Canada chief executive Jim Stanford.

Also, Petro-Canada late last year sold forward half of its 1996 crude oil production at US$18.04 a barrel, forcing the company to sit on the sidelines as many other oil companies reaped the benefit of the stronger than expected prices.
Petro-Canada said the hedging activities in its exploration and production division translated into C$32 million in foregone earnings.
In the company's refining and marketing division, third-quarter earnings from operations fell to C$23 million from C$62 million last year.

It said a five percent increase in refined product sales and lower operating costs did not offset the impact of the higher feedstock costs and lower retail prices that hit Canada's integrateds this year when Quebec became a battleground for price competition.

Third-quarter operating earnings in Petro-Canada's upstream division fell to C$22 million from C$35 million in 1995. It said increased depreciation, depletion and amortization charges from its acquisition this year of Amerada Hess Canada, and hedging activites erased much of the gains from higher prices and increased production volumes.
